responsibility: Implements Rust’s MIR-based borrow checker and its public query/consumer surface, turning MIR plus function signature lifetime information into verified borrow, move, mutability, and lifetime results, optional Polonius facts, and user diagnostics. The crate root in `lib.rs` orchestrates the full `mir_borrowck` pipeline and shared top-level state; `nll.rs` provides the main non-lexical-lifetime entry points that renumber MIR regions, run MIR type checking and region inference, and package inferred region/opaque-type/closure results. Setup for NLL is handled by `renumber.rs`, which replaces MIR regions with fresh inference variables, and `universal_regions.rs`, which extracts the body’s universal/free regions and signature environment. MIR borrow-check type analysis lives in `type_check`, which checks MIR against signatures and user types, proves predicates via type ops, and produces outlives constraints, member constraints, placeholders, type tests, and liveness inputs; `constraint_generation.rs` adds MIR-derived liveness plus Polonius control-flow and kill facts; `def_use.rs` supplies the def/use/drop classification those liveness computations rely on. The crate’s region-constraint solving core is split across `constraints`, which stores and graph-views NLL outlives constraints and SCC structure, `member_constraints.rs`, which tracks member constraints used especially for opaque types, and `region_infer`, which solves liveness and outlives constraints, computes region values and universal-region bounds, resolves opaque types, and exposes MIR/Graphviz introspection. To reason about borrows themselves, `borrow_set.rs` builds the canonical inventory of MIR borrows, including two-phase borrow reservation/activation data and per-local indexing; `path_utils.rs`, `prefixes.rs`, `place_ext.rs`, and `places_conflict.rs` provide the place/path utilities, prefix walking, borrow-trackability tests, and overlap/conflict rules that make borrow reasoning precise and sound. Runtime borrow-state propagation is performed by `dataflow.rs`, which tracks in-scope loans together with initializedness; `used_muts.rs` feeds borrowck information back into the `unused_mut` lint. For Polonius integration and fact export, `facts.rs` defines the rustc fact vocabulary and serializers, `location.rs` provides dense precise program-point indexing, and `invalidation.rs` derives `loan_invalidated_at` facts by replaying MIR accesses against conflict rules. The consumer-facing API in `consumers.rs` exposes rerunning borrow checking to obtain MIR, borrow sets, region inference results, and optional fact tables. User-facing reporting is handled by `diagnostics`, which analyzes causes, names regions/variables, accumulates suggestions, and emits tailored explanations, while `borrowck_errors.rs` centralizes construction of direct borrowck diagnostics and `session_diagnostics.rs` defines the structured diagnostic payload types. Together these modules make `rustc_borrowck` the compiler component that enforces Rust’s aliasing and lifetime rules on MIR, solves NLL region constraints, optionally interfaces with Polonius, and translates the results into compiler queries, analysis data, lints, and actionable error messages.
